vr-portfolio-1-demo-1-q05.backText:
Short quiz answer

A normal map perturbs the lighting normal to create the appearance of surface detail without changing geometry. Our corrugation normal map changes highlights; the emission map makes selected strips appear bright.

How our project does it

It changes the normal used in lighting, not the silhouette or geometry. RGB stores tangent-space directions and is interpreted as linear data. The corrugation texture changes visible highlights. An emission map marks a strip as bright; it does not illuminate surrounding geometry in this renderer.

Understand the idea

  • A normal is a direction perpendicular to a surface. Lighting uses it to decide how the surface faces the light.
  • Tangent-space normal-map RGB encodes direction relative to the textured surface. It is linear vector data, not colour that should receive an sRGB colour conversion.
  • The cabin can look ridged while keeping the same silhouette and triangle count. Emission does not cast light onto nearby surfaces in this renderer; the point/spot lights do that.

vr-portfolio-1-demo-1-q04.backText:
Short quiz answer

The custom cabin’s four wall quads each occupy one-quarter of the texture’s U range, with V running bottom-to-top. Separate wall vertices allow independent UVs and face normals.

How our project does it

cabin.js authors four tapered wall quads. Each wall's four UV corners occupy a quarter of the texture's U axis, with V from bottom to top. Adjacent geometric walls have separate vertices so they can have separate normal/UV values. Each quad is two indexed triangles. Floor/roof are separate meshes.

Understand the idea

  • UV coordinates are 2D addresses on a texture. U is horizontal and V is vertical; a 3D wall’s vertices tell the renderer which pixels to stretch across it.
  • Wall 0 uses U=0–0.25, wall 1 uses 0.25–0.5, wall 2 uses 0.5–0.75 and wall 3 uses 0.75–1. Each wall consists of two triangles.
  • Duplicating corner vertices across wall boundaries permits a UV seam and a different surface normal for each flat wall. The floor and roof are separate meshes.
